verdict.rationale: Greptile documents team-specific custom rules, uploading style guides, and repo-specific standards in greptile.json. It also imports existing rule files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, cursor.rules), lets you create coding patterns via MCP, and can scope rules to the directories each team owns. That covers natural-language rules and linked style guides as inputs to review. missing for 10: no evidence of AST/structural pattern rules, no detail on how strictly rules are enforced, no independent or hands-on corroboration of rule enforcement.

support.subject: As an engineering lead, I encode my team's own review guidelines — natural-language rules, AST patterns, or linked style guides — and the reviewer enforces them

citations.quote: Create custom rules that catch team-specific issues
Create custom rules, upload style guides, and configure repository-specific standards via greptile.json.
Automatically index existing rule files like Claude.md, AGENTS.md, and cursor.rules for richer review context.
Scope review settings, rules, and context to the directories each team owns.
With MCP, you can view, search, and create patterns from your IDE.
